Bridge sample comparison plot (Bland-Altman or scatter)

Source: R/plot_bridge.R
plot_bridge.Rd

Evaluates bridging reference samples measured across two Olink batches, plates, or studies. Given either two data objects (`data1`, `data2`) sharing common bridge `SampleID`s and `Assay`s, or a single data object with a `batch_col` column containing two batches, computes per-(sample, assay) paired NPX values and draws either a Bland-Altman difference-vs-mean plot (`type = "bland_altman"`, default) or an identity scatter plot (`type = "scatter"`).

Usage

plot_bridge(
  data1,
  data2 = NULL,
  batch_col = NULL,
  batches = NULL,
  type = c("bland_altman", "scatter"),
  assay_col = NULL,
  value_col = NULL,
  sample_col = NULL,
  panel_col = NULL,
  palette = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  ...
)

Arguments

data1

A data.frame in long format or an OlinkExperiment. If `data2` is `NULL`, `data1` must contain a `batch_col` column with two levels (or two batches selected via `batches`).

data2

Optional second data.frame in long format or OlinkExperiment representing the second batch/plate.

batch_col

Name of the batch or plate column when `data2` is `NULL`. If `NULL`, auto-detected from `Batch`, `PlateID`, `Plate`, or `Project`.

batches

Optional length-2 character vector naming the two levels of `batch_col` to compare when `data2` is `NULL`.

type

`"bland_altman"` (default; difference `batch2 - batch1` vs mean NPX with mean bias and 95 percent limits of agreement) or `"scatter"` (`batch2` vs `batch1` with identity line and Pearson r).

assay_col, value_col, sample_col, panel_col

Optional column names. If `NULL`, auto-detected.

palette

Optional color palette for panels/assays.

title

Plot title.

...

Additional arguments passed to `ggplot2::geom_point()`.

Value

A ggplot object. `p$data` contains the paired bridge measurements with columns `SampleID`, `Assay`, `.panel`, `.npx1`, `.npx2`, `.mean`, and `.diff`.

Examples

# \donttest{
# Compare two plates sharing overlapping sample IDs
b1 <- probc[probc$Timepoint == 1, ]
b2 <- b1
b2$NPX <- b1$NPX + rnorm(nrow(b1), mean = 0.15, sd = 0.2)
plot_bridge(b1, b2)

plot_bridge(b1, b2, type = "scatter")

# }
